overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated Shorts shows clear genre polarization: extreme planetary what-if survival scenarios and extreme celestial body profiles generate FACTVERSE's highest traction (averaging 700-1,050+ views with healthy 3.5-4% like-to-view ratios). Conversely, repetitive psychology facts (fake memories, earworms) and recycled trivia re-uploads suffer severe algorithmic fatigue, frequently bottoming out under 50 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: Second-Person Extreme Planet Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes) dominate top engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Prioritize second-person survival immersion hooks highlighting extreme planetary hazards and violent physical consequences.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) sustain high interest without fatigue.
winning_patterns.action: Frame celestial anomalies through stark, mind-bending sensory comparisons (e.g., metallic skies, radioactive auroras, mirror worlds).

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated uploads of 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (118, 183, 363 views) and 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' (34, 87, 220 views) fail to break out and split audience reach.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict uniqueness rules; retire topics after initial coverage unless an entirely new storytelling angle is deployed.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (3 uploads averaging 22 views) and 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) show negligible viewer retention and zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: Pause generic human psychology trivia in favor of cinematic survival, mystery micro-stories, or extreme astrophysics.
